objectives: Segment short-/e/ CVC words into phonemes.
Map each phoneme to the appropriate grapheme.
Spell taught short-/e/ CVC words accurately.
Use read-back to verify sound-to-letter encoding.
concepts: Encoding moves from spoken sounds to written graphemes.
Short /e/ is represented by e in the taught CVC pattern.
Each sound should be represented in sequence before the word is reread.

definitions.definition: Representing spoken sounds with written letters or graphemes.
Separating a word into its individual phonemes.
Matching each heard phoneme to the grapheme used to represent it.

workedExamples: pan versus pen → compare the middle /a/ and /e/ before writing.
commonMistakes: Using i or a instead of e.
Not reading the completed word back.
revisionPoints: spoken word → phonemes → graphemes → written word

basic: Segment and spell short-/e/ CVC words.
conceptual: Identify which grapheme represents the vowel phoneme.
application: Spell dictated short-/e/ CVC words using sound boxes or oral segmentation.
higherOrderThinking: Diagnose a vowel spelling error and select the correct repair.
mixedReview: Mix short-/e/ encoding with familiar short-vowel contrasts.

quickRevision: Say → segment → map → write → read back.
mistakeBasedRevision: e/a confusion → compare middle phonemes before writing.
weakTopicRevision: Repeat sound-to-letter mapping for the middle vowel in fresh CVC words.

activities.name: Sound-box encoding
steps: Push one counter for each sound.
Replace each counter with its letter.

outcomes: Learner segments taught short-/e/ CVC words accurately.
Learner maps short /e/ to e in the middle position.
Learner spells taught short-/e/ CVC words with accurate phoneme-grapheme correspondence.
Learner detects and repairs a vowel encoding error by rereading the word.
